guard: the manager's cooperative stop joins queued event work before it exits
why: The joins are what make a cooperative stop WAIT, boundedly, for event work it has already queued
before it exits, which is what C1 and C3 grade. That is narrower than a claim that nothing may
publish after teardown, and the narrower one is the true one: admitted work outliving the 1s intake
bound, and event work outliving the 10s swap bound, can both land afterwards, and both bounds say
so where they fire. The join went into the plugin-unload path first while the manager's stop ran a
separate routine that exited without joining, so even the narrow claim was false exactly where it
mattered. Both ways out now call one shared teardown, whose intake and event waits are bounded.
THE TWO JOINS COVER DIFFERENT CASES AND ARE GRADED SEPARATELY. The holder join covers event work
already running; the chain join covers a swap queued but not yet begun. C1 removes both and grades
that the teardown joins anything at all. C3 removes only the chain join, which the running case
cannot detect because the holder join catches it, and is reddened by the queued case instead.
C4 GRADES THE ORDER, NOT SUFFICIENCY AGAINST THE REAL KILL, and that boundary is measured rather
than assumed. A leg that stopped a seat and killed it after a short grace was built twice and
discarded twice, because it passed on BOTH arms: losing the connection purges the presence entry,
so a roster read after a kill says offline whether or not the seat published it, and a read taken
before the kill did not redden either. Cells that cannot fail are worse than absent ones, so it is
not here. What remains graded is that presence does not queue behind the drain.
C6 GRADES THE FENCE, C7 AND C8 GRADE THE WIRING, and they are different claims. C6 asks whether
the refusal refuses; C7 and C8 ask whether a given door actually goes THROUGH it, which is the
failure a shared guard is meant to prevent and which no amount of grading the guard itself can
see. Both are needed because a helper nothing routes to is a helper that guards nothing.
chat.message IS FENCED BUT NOT GRADED, stated rather than left to be discovered. Its only
connector-owned, presence-visible effect after teardown is a card-model publish, and that
publish carries the STORED status, which is already offline, so there is no presence-visible
harm to key a cell on. A prompt submitted natively in the host still starts a model turn whose
continuation this probe cannot observe, because the probe calls the closure directly; #687
records that. The probe knocks on it so the door is exercised, but mutating it out of the
table would survive, and no claim here covers it.
C9 IS A FOURTH DOOR AND NOT A FOURTH COPY OF THE SAME ONE. The tool map never passes through
the hook table: OpenCode is handed those closures at registration, so fencing the table left
them open. It is graded through cotal_status because that is the cotal_* tool with a
presence-visible effect; the others are fenced by the same wrapper but their harm is a channel
write, which this harness does not watch.
C10 ASKS WHETHER THE WAIT HAPPENS, C11 AND C12 WHETHER EACH DOOR IS IN IT. Same two-claim shape
as the fence: a wait nothing is registered with waits for nothing, and grading the wait alone
cannot see a door that never registers. C12 is not a duplicate of C11 because the two paths reach
presence differently, the hook through the plugin's helper and the tool straight to the agent.
THE CROSSING CELL RELEASES INSIDE THE BOUND, ON PURPOSE. The wait is bounded, so a straggler held
past it is released after departure by design and no mutation should be able to claim otherwise.
What is graded is the ORDER for work released while the teardown is still waiting. Holding it
longer would grade an unbounded wait that this fix does not claim to make.
SEAT-PREFIXED ASSERTION TEXT IS LOAD-BEARING. expectRed is a substring search over the whole
transcript, so two seats printing the same sentence would let the tool mutation match a red the
hook seat produced and report a kill for a door it never exercised. A false KILL is worse than a
survivor, because a survivor announces itself.
THE ORDERING IS SAMPLED BEFORE THE RELEASE, NOT AFTER IT. Looking for an inversion afterwards does
not work: with the wait removed, departure and the straggler both land between two polls, so the
parent never sees the intermediate offline, and the next offline it sees is the one agent.stop
publishes at the end, by which time the inversion has been repaired by the code under test. That
cell read GREEN against a broken implementation, and it is why C10 first came back WRONG-RED.
THREE PRESENCE WRITERS, THREE SEATS, THREE MUTATIONS. The model record publishes presence without
passing through the status helper, so it is a third path and not a variant of the other two. It
was very nearly shipped as tracked-but-ungraded on the argument that it cannot choose a status and
its write is submitted first; that argument may be sound, but it rests on the endpoint's KV write
ordering, which is a layer this file does not own, so it is proven instead of argued.
THE ENVIRONMENT SCRUB IS NOT MUTATION-GRADED, AND CANNOT HONESTLY BE. The suite gives each seat a
base environment with the COTAL_ and OPENCODE_ prefixes removed, because a launch spec only
overrides the keys it sets and everything else survives into the child. That matters: run from
inside a meshed session, the inherited model pin is authoritative to the connector, so it never
records a runtime model and the seat grading that publish cannot make one.
A mutation reverting the scrub would report SURVIVED wherever that variable happens to be unset,
which is every CI run, so its verdict would depend on who executed it rather than on the code. A
verdict that changes with the operator is worse than no verdict, because a survivor is supposed to
be a finding. Measured by hand instead, both directions, and recorded here so it is checkable by
rerunning rather than by trusting this note: with the environment scrubbed the model seat parks and
the suite is 22/0; with it inherited, on a box where the pin is set, the park control fails and the
ordering cell reads offline.
C14 IS NOT A VARIANT OF C10. C10 asks whether the teardown waits at all; C14 asks whether the wait
is for the SET or merely for the first thing that happens to it. A bare Promise.all rejects as soon
as one call does, and settleWithin counts any settlement including a rejection as done, so a single
failure released departure while another call was still parked. Every one of C10 through C13 passed
against that, because each of them parks exactly one caller and a set of one cannot show the
difference. It took a second call that FAILS, in the same seat, to make the distinction visible.
since Promise.all short-circuits on the first rejection to OCCUR rather than on a slot, so the two
arms are not two ways for the defect to appear. What the pair pins is that the wait reaches both ENDS
of the set: one arm has the failing call at the tail, the other at the head.
WHAT THE PAIR DOES NOT PIN, and a review proved this by live mutation rather than by argument: a
repair absorbing only `i === 0 || i === all.length - 1` passes BOTH arms and the whole suite, because
in a set of two every index is already an end. An earlier version of this file claimed the two arms
caught any partial wrap. They did not. C17 and the interior seat exist because of that measurement:
three admitted calls with the failing one in the middle is the smallest set that HAS an interior.
THE IMPLEMENTATION NO LONGER HAS THAT DEGREE OF FREEDOM, which is why the seats stop carrying the
universal. The hand-rolled per-element map was replaced with `Promise.allSettled`: it waits for every
element and never rejects, so partial absorption is not a state this code can express. C14 through
C17 therefore grade a REGRESSION rather than a property. Each replaces allSettled with a different
hand-rolled wait, and each is caught by the seat whose shape that wait fails. None of them, and no
finite set of seats, establishes elementwise absorption for every length; the primitive does.
C18 IS THE ONE DOOR THAT WAS ALREADY PAST THE CHECK. Every other cell here parks work that has yet
to be refused, or work that reaches presence. C18 parks a TURN SUBMISSION: drive reads its phase
guards and then awaits session creation, so the read and the submit are separated by a server round
trip, and a drive admitted while the seat was healthy resumes inside teardown. A reviewer
reproduced that live before this cell existed, and the first version of the cell was VACUOUS: with
nothing else parked, quiesce had an empty intake set and the process exited before the drive could
resume, so the seat went green on a tree with the defect still in it. The seat now parks a tool
call as well, which is what holds the teardown open long enough for the window to be real. That is
also why the precondition is its own cell: if the parked call is not there, the result below grades
nothing. A SURVIVED on C18 means the window closed again, not that the code is safe.
C19 SEPARATES REFUSED FROM DROPPED, which no prompt count can do on its own: not submitting and
losing the caller's input are both zero prompts. It is graded on the CUTOVER arm of the refusal and
not the stop arm, and that is measured rather than stylistic. A cross-incarnation version was built
and removed: a replacement seat, on a fresh lifecycle uid and then on the same one, drove at once on
a newly sent DM but never received the refused one, so a batch held at teardown does not survive the
process. Durability across a stop is a delivery question and is not claimed here.
C20 IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS, found by a reviewer after the first two were fixed:
drive losing its caller's input on an early return. It is the narrowest of the three and the one
with no second copy anywhere. A focus @mention is acked-and-dropped at ingest, so it is not in the
inbox and pendingForWake() cannot see it; the nudge string exists only in the call that carries it.
What is lost is the WAKE and not the message, whose body stays recallable through cotal_inbox, so
the seat is simply never told to go and look. The cell needs the seat to be IN FOCUS or an
@mention is an ordinary batch and there is no nudge to lose, which is why that precondition is
graded rather than assumed: the first version of this leg set focus once at boot, before the link
was up, the call did not take, and the cell graded the batch path twice while claiming to grade
nudges.

mutations.name: C1 the shared teardown stops joining the event work at all, so a stop abandons a drain that was already in flight
mutations.find:
await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
    await settleWithin(events?.settled(), SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "event holder at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: cooperative stop joined the queued event work before exiting

mutations.name: C2 a turn may start mid-cutover again, so an ordinary inbound message prompts the new session before its replacement holder is installed
mutations.find: const phaseClosed = (): boolean => stopping || swapping;
mutations.expectRed: no turn was started while the cutover was open

mutations.name: C3 the teardown joins only the holder, so a swap that was still QUEUED when the stop arrived is abandoned unrun
mutations.find: await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: a swap still QUEUED at the stop was allowed to run before exit

mutations.name: C4 leaving the mesh queues behind the drain again, so a seat whose drain outlives the runtime's grace window is killed before its presence goes offline
mutations.find:
await safeStatus("offline");
    await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
mutations.replace:
await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
    await safeStatus("offline");
mutations.expectRed: the seat left the mesh BEFORE the drain finished, not behind it

mutations.name: C5 teardown stops being a refusal, so the swap's deferred drive starts a NEW turn while the stop is still joining the chain, after presence has gone offline
mutations.find: const phaseClosed = (): boolean => stopping || swapping;
mutations.expectRed: the teardown started no turn of its own after the stop began

mutations.find: async (...args: never[]): Promise<unknown> => (stopping ? undefined : await hook(...args)),
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.name: C7 the tool hook is wired past the fence instead of through it, which is exactly the omission a single shared guard is supposed to make impossible
mutations.find: ...fence(intake),
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.name: C8 the event hook is wired past the fence instead of through it, so a late permission.asked republishes presence over the offline record
mutations.find: ...fence(intake),
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.find: stopping ? `⚠ ${name} was not run: this seat is shutting down` : await track(def.execute(...args)),
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.expectRed: hook-seat: departure was still unpublished while admitted work was in flight

mutations.find: if (agent.connected) await track(agent.setStatus(status, activity));
mutations.expectRed: hook-seat: departure was still unpublished while admitted work was in flight

mutations.find: stopping ? `⚠ ${name} was not run: this seat is shutting down` : await track(def.execute(...args)),

mutations.expectRed: tool-seat: departure was still unpublished while admitted work was in flight

mutations.name: C14 the wait goes back to Promise.all over the raw calls, which is the defect as it shipped: one rejection satisfies it and departure publishes while another call is still parked
mutations.find: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.allSettled([...inFlight]), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.replace: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.all([...inFlight]), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: hook-seat: departure was still unpublished while admitted work was in flight

mutations.name: C15 absorption is hand-rolled again and covers only the FIRST admitted call, so a failure anywhere behind it still ends the wait early
mutations.find: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.allSettled([...inFlight]), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.replace: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.all([...inFlight].map((work, i) => (i === 0 ? work.then(() => undefined, () => undefined) : work))), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: hook-seat: departure was still unpublished while admitted work was in flight

mutations.name: C16 absorption is hand-rolled again and covers only the LAST admitted call, so a failure at the head of the set still ends the wait early
mutations.find: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.allSettled([...inFlight]), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.replace: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.all([...inFlight].map((work, i, all) => (i === all.length - 1 ? work.then(() => undefined, () => undefined) : work))), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: mirror-seat: departure was still unpublished while admitted work was in flight

mutations.name: C17 absorption is hand-rolled again and covers only the ENDS of the set, the shape a review proved could pass every two-call cell, so only an interior failure shows it
mutations.find: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.allSettled([...inFlight]), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.replace: const settled = await settleWithin(Promise.all([...inFlight].map((work, i, all) => (i === 0 || i === all.length - 1 ? work.then(() => undefined, () => undefined) : work))), INTAKE_SETTLE_MS, "admitted intake at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: interior-seat: an interior failure did not release departure while parked work remained
